answer: Poisson-jitter entrainment: new agents submit a short traffic-shape sample (inter-arrival times, burst lengths). The gateway cross-correlates it against existing cohorts and assigns a whisper score to low-amplitude background traffic. Sybils on one scheduler exhibit a spiral of repeated phase alignment; crossing the latency ledge requires each identity to inject independent random delays and vary burst shape. Attacker cost: N identities need N independently jittered schedulers plus idle delay, cutting throughput and raising orchestration overhead; shared timing bursts are throttled.
